diagnosis.root_cause: In chat_stream (patient/api_gateway/app/main.py:478), the else-branch that titles a new session reads `len(req.qestion)`, which misspells `question`. ChatRequest (main.py:84-88) declares only session_id, question, collection_name and stream, with no `qestion` field or alias. Pydantic's BaseModel.__getattr__ therefore raises AttributeError. The exception is unhandled, so the ASGI middleware answers 500. The branch runs only when there is no session_id and the question has no '?'. That explains why only a fraction of /api/chat requests (~6-10% of gateway traffic) fail while traffic stays flat. The same typo was introduced earlier by commit 19871dd and reverted, and commit d0ba09a has reintroduced it. Minimal fix: on line 478, change `len(req.qestion)` to `len(req.question)`. The doctor's secondary hypothesis, a restart during rollout, would only cause transient errors and needs no code change.
evidence: patient/api_gateway/app/main.py:478: `title = req.question.strip()[:60] + ("..." if len(req.qestion) > 60 else "")` uses the misspelled attribute `qestion`
patient/api_gateway/app/main.py:475-476: questions containing '?' take the other branch, which uses `req.question` correctly, so only questions without '?' fail
patient/api_gateway/app/main.py:84-88: ChatRequest defines only session_id, question, collection_name and stream, with no `qestion` field or alias
patient/api_gateway/app/main.py:472: the titling block runs only for new sessions (no session_id), so follow-up messages are unaffected
Stack trace: AttributeError "'ChatRequest' object has no attribute 'qestion'" raised from pydantic __getattr__ called at main.py:478 in chat_stream; logs show this error x18
bugs:20261122-090542-0a4683 records the identical typo from commit 19871dd earlier the same day, so this is a regression
faults/acceptance/test_f5_typo.py:4-6 posts a question without '?' ('hostel curfew timings') and expects 200; it would fail on the current code and pass after the fix

patch.diff:
diff --git a/patient/api_gateway/app/main.py b/patient/api_gateway/app/main.py
--- a/patient/api_gateway/app/main.py
+++ b/patient/api_gateway/app/main.py
@@ -475,7 +475,7 @@
         if "?" in req.question:
             title = req.question.split("?")[0].strip()[:60] + "?"
         else:
-            title = req.question.strip()[:60] + ("..." if len(req.qestion) > 60 else "")
+            title = req.question.strip()[:60] + ("..." if len(req.question) > 60 else "")
         cursor.execute("INSERT INTO chat_sessions (id, title, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (session_id, title, datetime.utcnow().isoformat()))
         conn.commit()
patch.rationale: Commit d0ba09a reintroduced a typo in the new-session titling branch of chat_stream (patient/api_gateway/app/main.py:478). That line calls `len(req.qestion)`, but ChatRequest only defines `question`. Pydantic therefore raises AttributeError for every new session (no session_id) whose question has no '?', and the gateway returns a 500. The fix changes that attribute to `req.question`. The titling feature stays as it is, and the '?' branch is untouched. This matches the earlier accepted fix for the same regression (bugs:20261122-090542-0a4683). The find string includes the full line, which is unique in the file. faults/acceptance/test_f5_typo.py posts a question without '?' and expects 200, so it should pass with this change. No tests were modified.
